topics.topic: Whether Registry must reject bindable addresses that could expose a surface outside the permitted networks or leave reachability enforcement to host administration
questions: Does Registry merely bind every syntactically valid configured address, leaving the stated reachability entirely to host administration, or must it refuse a configured address whose binding can expose a surface through another interface; and, if it must refuse it, how can it determine that condition?

Must Registry reject an otherwise well-formed, bindable address that exposes a surface beyond the stated network, or are those reachability limits enforced only by host networking and therefore outside Registry's checks?

Must Registry reject a syntactically valid bind address, such as a wildcard or an address on another interface, when that address could make a surface reachable outside the stated networks, or does Registry validate only the address syntax and leave all reachability enforcement to host administration?

quotes:
The addresses are the deployment's: the
   service API is reachable only in VM Platform and over the WireGuard
   channel from the VPS, the owner interface only through the owner's VPN
   (R0-28, R0-29, R0-48), and the interface each is bound to on that host,
   or on a test instance's (R0-34), is the host's administration — so the
   configuration names them

The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: the service tokens and the
   service API's address all five or none — none makes an owner-only start,
   and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; the two addresses'
   ports different; each secret's length (rule 3);
   their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule
   5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary
   prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.
judgement.why: Registry checks syntax and bindability at the configured address, while selection and network reachability of the bound interface belong to host administration.

topics.topic: Whether required tests must verify all allowed and forbidden reachability paths or treat the network boundary as an external host-administration fact
questions: What Required tests item must show that each surface is reachable through every allowed path and through no forbidden path, or state that this is an external host-administration fact not asserted by State 2 tests?

judgement.why: The network paths are explicitly assigned to host administration, so State 2's Registry tests need not prove the deployment topology's allowed and forbidden reachability paths.

topics.topic: Whether the stated network reachability restrictions also apply to test instances
questions: Do the VM Platform, WireGuard and owner-VPN reachability restrictions apply only to production, or must a test instance also expose its surfaces only through those networks?
